description: The close error arm reached with ZERO records read. CUSTFILE is declared as a dataset that exists and holds no row - "empty": true together with its 500-byte recordLength and its CVCUS01Y copybook - and that declaration is deliberate and load-bearing rather than an unfinished fixture: a dataset a case says nothing about is omitted from "inputs" altogether, an inline row list with no rows in it declares neither, and only the empty declaration reaches the branch a unit takes when its first READ meets end of file. A single blank 500-space row would not serve either, because a blank row is a record and this would then be a one-record case rather than an empty-dataset one. Trace: L71 displays the opening banner. 0000-CUSTFILE-OPEN puts 8 into APPL-RESULT at L119 and opens INPUT; an existing empty dataset opens cleanly, so the test at L121 sees '00', L122 moves 0, the 88 APPL-AOK at L126 holds, and the paragraph CONTINUEs without emitting a line - that transient 8 is overwritten before anything can observe it. The PERFORM UNTIL at L74 tests its condition first, and END-OF-FILE is still 'N' from its VALUE clause at L65, so the body runs exactly once. 1000-CUSTFILE-GET-NEXT reads at L93 and gets '10': L94's test for '00' fails, so the display sitting inside that arm at L96 never runs; L98's test for '10' holds and L99 moves 16 into APPL-RESULT; APPL-AOK is false at L104, so control reaches L107 where the 88 APPL-EOF - VALUE 16 - holds, and L108 moves 'Y' into END-OF-FILE. The fatal read arm at L110-L113 is not taken, so the read paragraph's own error literal, the status line it would have rendered and the abend banner beneath them are all absent. Back in the mainline the second guard at L77 now fails, and that is precisely why no record line appears: the display at L78 is not missing from the program, it is refused by the guard. The loop condition is re-evaluated, END-OF-FILE is 'Y', and the loop ends. 9000-CUSTFILE-CLOSE is then performed from L83: L137's ADD 8 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT resets the register, the CLOSE at L138 reports '42' - the status a close against a file that is not open reports - so the '00' test at L139 fails, L142's ADD 12 TO ZERO GIVING puts 12 into APPL-RESULT, the 88 APPL-AOK at L144 is false, and the error arm at L147-L150 displays 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE', moves CUSTFILE-STATUS into IO-STATUS, renders it through Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS and performs Z-ABEND-PROGRAM, which displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at L155, moves 0 to TIMING and 999 to ABCODE, and calls CEE3ABD at L158. Four lines exactly, and no fifth: L158 ends the enclave inside the close, so control never returns from the PERFORM at L83, the closing banner at L85 is never displayed and GOBACK at L87 never runs. The open succeeded silently, so the open paragraph's DD-named error literal is absent as well; all three of this program's error literals are distinct and only the close's appears here. THE POINT, AND IT IS A SINGLE VARIABLE: case04.json declares the very same empty CUSTFILE and takes the very same clean path through the open, the zero-iteration record pass and the end-of-file transition, and differs from this case in nothing but what the CLOSE at L138 answers. There it answers '00', L140's SUBTRACT APPL-RESULT FROM APPL-RESULT leaves zero, the run reaches L85 and ends normally with two lines and RETURN-CODE 0; here it answers '42' and the run ends with four lines, no closing banner and RETURN-CODE 12. If both cases pass, the close outcome is genuinely what drives the difference; if only one passes, the failure points straight at the close branch rather than at anything else in the program. AND WHAT PAIRING WITH case18.json PROVES: case18 fails the same CLOSE with the same '42' after three complete record pairs, this case after none, and both must produce the same three trailing lines and the same RETURN-CODE 12. That is the assertion that 9000-CUSTFILE-CLOSE is independent of record-processing state, and the source makes it true by construction - L137's ADD 8 TO ZERO GIVING resets APPL-RESULT on entry regardless of what the read loop left in it. Here the loop left 16, the 88 APPL-EOF value; in case18 it left 16 as well; in neither does that value survive into the close decision. An implementation that carried APPL-RESULT forward instead of resetting it could pass one of the two and fail the other. RETURN-CODE 12 comes from L142 and from nowhere else on this path: the 8 at L137 is a dead store overwritten on both arms, and the 16 the end-of-file read leaves is loop-control state this program never moves to RETURN-CODE - CBCUS01C contains no reference to RETURN-CODE anywhere, so 0 and 12 are the only two codes derivable from it. The rendered status line is 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0042' and is byte-identical to case18's, as it must be. Two things about it are quirks of the source and both are preserved (practice B5): the literal at L168 and L172 is 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' and that NNNN is placeholder text nothing ever substitutes - it is emitted verbatim with the four-character image appended directly and no space between - and '42' is all-numeric with IO-STAT1 = '4' rather than '9', so the ELSE arm at L169-L173 applies: MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04 then MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2), which is '00' followed by '42', read mechanically from the IO-STATUS-04 declaration at L57-L59 (practice B11). The error line is the long-form 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE' of L147 and not a DD-named one: the open paragraph's literal at L129 names the DD instead, while the read and close paragraphs both name the CUSTOMER FILE, and that inconsistency is the source's and stays. Coverage: this is the one case in the folder that drives 88 APPL-EOF true, on the read, and 88 APPL-AOK false, on the close, in the same run (gate G50), and it is the second CLOSE-to-other outcome the folder declares - distinct from case18's by record count rather than by status value (gate G47). It also covers OPEN to '00' and READ to '10', and does not cover READ to '00' at all, because no record is ever delivered. No record line exists here, so this case asserts no 500-byte record width and no FILLER span - cases 01 and 11 own gates G19 and G21 - and it declares no dataset-level expectation either, because an arranged backend answers from a stub and no final state is read back for one to be compared against. The unit is customer.CustomerFileReaderJob driven at Tasklet and step level with no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path (gate G51), with customer.CustomerService holding the decisions - it independently fixes returnCode 12, abcode 999 and timing 0. Nothing is written: expectedWrites is empty as the positive assertion that a program whose whole function is 'Read and print customer data file' issues no WRITE and no REWRITE, and CustomerFileReaderJob is a Job by name only (AAP rule R1). The '42' the CLOSE reports is arranged in the scenario table of CBCUS01CParityTest, because a BATCH_JOB case cannot carry a ForcedOutcome - that member belongs to ParityCase.ScreenRequest - and the arranged input and the expected output are written independently of each other. The seeded dataset's code page is US-ASCII, named explicitly and never left to the platform (practice B8). Provenance, practice B12: every expected value here is statically derived from app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl, the byte layout of app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy and the DD and PARM contract of app/jcl/READCUST.jcl, whose STEP05 is a bare EXEC PGM=CBCUS01C with no PARM - hence the empty jobParameters. None of it was captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler as disabled, and no Language Environment CEE* services exist, so CEE3ABD itself cannot be called. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted - the twenty cases per program, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate are all unchanged - and the substitution is escalated for explicit confirmation rather than absorbed (AAP section 0.7.6, risk R-A).
